"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate at current lines 1104-1116 checks for positive and changed manager PIDs and invocation IDs, but it never verifies that both snapshots come from the same boot. A guest reboot between those snapshots changes both PID and invocation ID, so the predicate can report an isolated manager restart even though the observations span a reboot. The same snapshot objects already carry boot_id in the reboot check at lines 1117-1124, so requiring nonempty equal manager boot IDs is a routine correctness fix rather than a new requirement.
